question: How are school proprietors and educational institutions categorized and regulated for taxes in Uganda?
answer: In Uganda, educational institutions are established across pre-primary, primary, secondary, tertiary, vocational, and university levels by either the Government, religious/charitable organizations, or private commercial proprietors. School proprietors have legal ownership of the educational entity and must register with: 1) Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) for business names or limited liability company incorporation; 2) Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) for institutional licensing and registration; 3) Local municipal councils (KCCA or town councils) for operating permits; 4) Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) to acquire a 10-digit TIN with obligations for Corporation Tax, PAYE, and Withholding Tax.

question: Are schools exempt from income tax in Uganda, and how are private commercial schools taxed?
answer: Schools are NOT automatically exempt from income tax in Uganda: 1) Non-Profit / Charitable Educational Institutions: Only public schools or institutions of a public educational character that possess a formal written exemption ruling from the Commissioner General under Section 21(1)(f) of the Income Tax Act are exempt from income tax (provided no part of the income confers private benefit to proprietors or trustees); 2) Private For-Profit Schools: Taxed at the standard thirty percent (30%) Corporation Income Tax (CIT) rate on net chargeable income (gross tuition fees, boarding fees, admission charges, and transport receipts less allowable operational costs such as teacher salaries, scholastic materials, food, utilities, and repairs); provisional returns are submitted twice yearly via Form DT-1001; 3) Sole Proprietor Schools: Taxed under graduated individual income tax brackets up to 40%.

question: What are the VAT exemptions and zero-rated supplies available to the education sector in Uganda?
answer: Under the Second and Third Schedules of the Value Added Tax Act: 1) Educational Services: The provision of educational services (tuition fees, examination fees, boarding fees directly provided by educational institutions) is strictly an exempt supply under Schedule 2 of the VAT Act; 2) Scholastic Materials: Textbooks, Bibles, Qu'rans, mathematical sets, geometry sets, crayons, colored pencils, lead pencils, rulers, erasers, stencils, technical drawing sets, educational computer tablets, educational software, and laboratory science chemicals are 100% exempt from VAT; 3) Exercise Books: Locally manufactured exercise books in Uganda or the EAC are VAT-exempt (imported exercise books attract 18% VAT); 4) Educational Materials Manufactured in EAC: Supplies of educational materials produced within Uganda or EAC Partner States are zero-rated (0% VAT).

question: What customs duty exemptions apply to scientific research apparatus, vocational training equipment, and sports vehicles?
answer: Under the EAC Common External Tariff (CET) and Fifth Schedule EACCMA: 1) Scientific Instruments (Florence Agreement Annex D): Scientific instruments and research apparatus intended exclusively for educational or pure scientific research consigned to approved educational institutions are exempt from all import duties and taxes; 2) Vocational Training Equipment: Woodworking machines, welding machines, and industrial sewing machines imported for vocational education attract 0% import duty under EAC CET and are VAT-exempt; 3) Textbooks & Religious Literature: Textbooks, Bibles, and Qu'rans attract 0% import duty and 0% VAT; 4) Sports Equipment: Specially designed rally cars and spare parts, racing motorcycles, and racing bicycles imported by licensed competitors/drivers are exempt from all taxes under the 5th Schedule EACCMA.

question: What major tax holidays and incentives apply to investors establishing vocational or technical institutes in Uganda?
answer: Under the Income Tax Act, VAT Act, and Stamp Duty Act: Investors who establish or operate vocational or technical institutes in an Industrial Park, Free Zone, or other approved site with an investment capital of at least USD 10 million (foreign investors), USD 300,000 (EAC citizens), or USD 150,000 (upcountry citizen investments) using 70%+ local raw materials/inputs and employing at least 70% EAC citizens (taking up 70%+ of the wage bill) enjoy: 1) A 10-year income tax holiday on institutional earnings; 2) No VAT on feasibility studies, architectural design, and locally produced materials; 3) Nil stamp duty on debentures, land leases, land transfers, and share capital increases; 4) Nil excise duty on facility construction materials.

question: What are the employment tax (PAYE) and Withholding Tax (WHT) obligations for schools in Uganda?
answer: 1) Pay As You Earn (PAYE): Every educational institution employing teachers, administrators, or support staff earning above the monthly statutory threshold (UGX 235,000 / revised UGX 335,000) must deduct PAYE and remit it monthly by the 15th of the following month via Form DT-1004; 2) Withholding Tax (WHT): Schools must withhold 6% WHT on payments for supplies of goods, materials (foodstuffs, uniforms, furniture), and services exceeding UGX 1,000,000 from non-exempt vendors and remit monthly via Form DT-1013; 3) Withholding on Payments to Teachers for Part-Time Services: Payments to external guest lecturers or non-salaried examiners attract WHT.
